analyst_view.overall: Second-tier Torreense (19th, 6 pts) host Celtic (32nd, 3 pts) in Leiria, about 60 km from home because their own ground does not meet UEFA rules. Torreense, under new coach João Nuno, won 3-2 against Ararat with a stoppage-time comeback but lose scorer Jorge Aguirre to the red card from that game (already counted by the numbers). Celtic need points badly after three defeats in four; Martin O'Neill's side won 4-1 against St Mirren on Saturday, but midfielder Mika Baur is out for about 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage and Benjamin Nygren missed the weekend with a heel problem; neither is in the numbers' list. No referee is named yet. I lean slightly lower on goals and shots on target for Celtic's missing attacking midfielders.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and already take 8% off Torreense's scoring for Aguirre's ban. They don't know Celtic are without Baur, a regular scorer from midfield, and maybe Nygren; Celtic still scored four on Saturday without both, so I trim only a little, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.9 corners and already add 7% for Celtic's recent corner count. Torreense defended deep and gave up the flanks when down to ten against Ararat, which fits a Celtic-heavy corner count the numbers already show, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.8 cards. Celtic chasing the game against a deep side can draw fouls, and Torreense picked up a red in their last European game, but recent card counts are already counted and no referee is named, so I stay at 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers expect 27.2 shots and already push Celtic's up about 9% because Torreense concede plenty. Celtic should have most of the ball; their creativity is a bit lower without Baur, but the volume should hold, so I stay at 27.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 8.9 shots on target. Without Baur's late runs into the box and with Nygren doubtful, Celtic's quality of chances drops a little, so I go to about 8.6.
